subject: POC streaming latency budget + operational handoff
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Dillon <alice.dillon@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: POC streaming latency budget + operational handoff

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so everyone has alignment before the POC window:

Summary of ask (from Finexa):
- Sustained streaming workload for real-time annotation of transaction events (avg payload ~1.6KB)
- 95th percentile per-token tail latency target: 120ms end-to-end on private deployment
- Concurrency target: ~160 concurrent streams during peak windows (bursts up to 300 for ~30s)
- Throughput: ~12k tokens/s sustained, spiking to 22k tokens/s for short bursts
- Requirement: VPN-based peering to our VPC with egress to internal model runtime (no public egress)

What Redwood will validate during the POC:
- End-to-end tail latency (client -> Finexa edge -> VPN -> model host) under the declared concurrency profile
- Streaming stability (prefix/KV cache behavior) with alternating long and short sequences
- Fallback behavior when peering bandwidth is constrained (graceful degrade to lower-q model variant)

Immediate next steps (action owners & timing):
1) Finexa to provide a small test workload generator + access to a staging endpoint (DevOps) — due Thu 6/10 EOD (Alice/DevOps)
2) Redwood to share a short diagnostics template and POC map showing test endpoints, required ports, and expected p99 probe script — by Thu 6/10 AM (Ben)
3) Run an initial smoke test (low concurrency) to validate tunnel/config and collect baseline latency — target Fri 6/11 (joint)
4) Ops handoff call to Finexa SREs with a short runbook and escalation path — Mon 6/14 10:00 PT (Priyom / Soojin)

Attachments: redwood-poc-map.pdf (POC topology + ports), network-diagnostics-template.csv (traceroute/iperf/MTU checklist)

If anything above looks off, flag it here. Otherwise I’ll schedule the handoff meeting and share the runbook by Friday.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priom_das@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: POC streaming latency budget + operational handoff

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) The 120ms p95 you listed is correct for our critical path (real-time risk scoring). For p99 we’re comfortable up to 200ms for the POC window.
2) Our DevOps will provision a staging endpoint reachable via the existing VPN peering; we’ll share credentials and a NAT IP for the tunnel.
3) Payloads can vary; while average is 1.6KB we’ll include frequent small messages (~200B) and occasional long traces (~6KB). Please ensure streaming handles wide variance.

We’re attaching two artifacts: a sample throughput profile (CSV) and our internal SRE runbook excerpt (PDF). We’ll aim to have the workload generator available by Thu 6/10 5pm PT.

One ask: can Redwood run an initial passive traceroute and TCP MST to validate MTU and asymmetric routing before Friday’s smoke test? If you can share the diagnostics template now we’ll populate it and send traces back.

Thanks —
Alice
Head of Integrations, Finexa
alice.dillon@finexa.com

Alice / Finexa DevOps —

Thanks — I’ve attached the network-diagnostics-template.csv we discussed (same file referenced in Priyom’s note). A few technical clarifications from the Redwood runtime side to make sure our measurements are comparable:

- End-to-end latency target needs a consistent measuring point. For the POC please capture timestamps at the Finexa staging endpoint immediately after enqueue (client-side) and at our model host ingress (we’ll provide an HTTP header echo timestamp). We’ll align on clock sync (NTP) during the handoff.
- For streaming (HTTP/2 or gRPC streaming), packetization and MTU matter. If your VPN MTU is < 1400 we may see >10% increase in per-token latency for the 6KB traces.
- Concurrency profile: please include a single steady-state run at 160 concurrent streams for 10 minutes, then repeat a spike run: ramp to 300 concurrent streams in 15s and hold for 30s, then drop — we’ll monitor tail behavior and KV cache hit rates.
- Egress rules: ensure outbound to our private tenancy IP range is permitted on TCP 443 and UDP 4500 for the tunnel. If there’s any NAT re-use or port-mapping at your edge let us know — it affects connection churn under bursts.

I’ve provisioned a short-lived test endpoint on our staging cluster: https://staging-poc.redwood.local/finexa-test (credentials to follow via secure token). We’ll also share a p99 probe script (small Go binary) that emits both small/large payloads and records per-token latencies.

Let me know when you populate the diagnostics csv and we’ll schedule the smoke test.

Cheers,
Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Perfect — thanks everyone. Action items consolidated:

- Finexa (Alice/DevOps): populate and return network-diagnostics-template.csv with traceroute/iperf results by EOD Thu 6/10. Provide staging endpoint details and a short SSH key or token for the test endpoint.
- Redwood (Ben): share the p99 probe script and the small-run smoke test schedule (we’ll propose windows Fri 6/11 9:00 PT and 14:00 PT; pick one).
- Redwood (Priyom / Soojin): prepare the ops handoff deck and runbook; will send invite for Mon 6/14 10:00 PT — will include escalation matrix, playbook for peering flaps, and downgrade flow to lower-Q model variant.

If finite changes crop up (e.g., MTU < 1400 or constrained egress), Ben will propose mitigation knobs (burst shaping, token-batching, client-side pacing) and we’ll validate in a follow-up test.

I’ll keep the HubSpot deal updated and attach the runbook and test results to the shared drive.

Thanks — looking forward to the smoke test.

Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
